intended_object: For a topological group G and open normal subgroups N ≤ M, the canonical continuous surjective homomorphism G/N → G/M, gN ↦ gM. These are the transition maps of the inverse system of discrete quotients (docstring and name).
explanation: The underlying map is `QuotientGroup.map N M (MonoidHom.id G)`, which is well defined because N ≤ M. This is exactly the canonical projection G/N → G/M. Continuity is proved by temporarily using the fact that G/N with its quotient topology is discrete when N is open (`QuotientGroup.discreteTopology N.isOpen`). That `letI` gives the same topology as the existing instance and is only used in the continuity proof. The setting is natural: any topological group with open normal subgroups, and the ring k is not used. Mathlib builds the same maps only inside the finite-quotient diagram functors for profinite groups (`ProfiniteGrp/Limits.lean`, `ProfiniteGrp/Completion.lean`), as `FiniteGrp` morphisms. It has no standalone continuous-hom version for general topological groups, so this definition is not a narrower copy of a Mathlib one.
